dedupe_keys.name: nat4wat tool and api for selecting nature based solutions for water treatment and runoff

description: Nat4Wat is a web tool that helps users select the most appropriate nature-based solutions for water treatment, storage and reuse and for runoff mitigation, given a case scenario. Users describe their case (water type and needs) and the tool selects suitable natural treatment systems such as treatment wetlands, drawing on a knowledge base of 54 solutions with their performance, co-benefits, barriers and costs, plus scientific publications and market cases. It is global in scope, with land needs given for tropical, dry, temperate and continental climates. The engine is a REST API written in express.js by Josep Pueyo-Ros (ICRA) and Joaquim Comas (University of Girona), released on Zenodo as version 1.0 on 22 May 2025 under the MIT licence, and developed in the MULTISOURCE project funded by the EU Horizon 2020 programme (grant 101003527). The web tool is free but asks users to log in or create an account. Caveats: the rankings rest on literature-derived performance ranges, not site design. It supports climate adaptation and green-blue infrastructure planning for wastewater and stormwater; a related record is the ICRA knowledge base of NBS for water treatment and stormwater management, which feeds it.
